# Cryptographic test-vector provenance

The immutable known answers in crypto_tests.cpp are public published fixtures,
not operational private keys. Do not use these keys outside tests.

- RFC 8439 section 2.8.2 (same vector as RFC 7539): ChaCha20-Poly1305 with
  32-byte key, 12-byte nonce, associated data and full ciphertext/tag.
  https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8439.html#section-2.8.2
- Three exact-block AEAD regressions copied from the pinned Botan 3.13.0
  `src/tests/data/aead/chacha20poly1305.vec`, whose provenance labels these as
  generated by OpenSSL. Expected outputs are upstream data, not GhostWire output.
- RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 1/2/3: empty, one-byte and two-byte pure Ed25519
  messages, seed/public key/signature. These also appear at the start of Botan's
  `src/tests/data/pubkey/ed25519.vec`.
  https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032.html#section-7.1
- Botan `src/tests/data/pubkey/ed25519_verify.vec`: invalid identity and
  noncanonical identity-element public-key/signature forgeries.
- Botan `src/tests/data/hash/sha2_32.vec`: SHA-256 empty, abc and the standard
  abcdbc...nopq padding-boundary vector (NIST/FIPS SHA examples).

The unmodified upstream files are retained in the signed, pinned source archive
under third_party/botan. Unit tests exercise GhostWire's real production facade.
Separate fault tests compile the same facade implementation with explicit private
test hooks. The Linux linker-wrap test exercises actual getrandom error handling
inside the production Botan and GhostWire libraries. No fallback RNG is installed
in an application binary. These tests do not prove protocol security or entropy
quality from output statistics, and are not a standalone cryptographic audit.
